relationships.subject: C-176
relationships.evidence_quote: Selective STING antagonist C-176 was administered and pain behaviors were assessed following spared nerve injury (SNI)-induced neuropathic pain.

relationships.subject: C-176
relationships.evidence_quote: Early but not the late intrathecal injection of C-176 attenuated SNI-induced pain hypersensitivity, microglia activation, proinflammatory factors, and phosphorylated JAK2/STAT3 in the spinal cord dorsal horn

relationships.subject: IL-6
relationships.evidence_quote: the analgesic effect of C-176 was greatly abolished by recombinant IL-6 following SNI

relationships.subject: STING
relationships.evidence_quote: dsDNA was significantly increased following SNI and STING/TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1)/nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) pathway was activated in vivo and vitro.

key_findings: Early blockade of STING with C-176 reduced SNI pain, microglial activation and JAK2/STAT3 phosphorylation in the dorsal horn
Microglial STING/TBK1/NF-κB drives pain initiation via IL-6 signaling
